report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a professional culinary assistant (chef/recipe generator), i.e., to produce cooking/recipe/kitchen guidance in a more “professional/technical” tone.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary: across high-norm cells (esp. later layers), top directions include “Cook”, “Cooking”, “culinary”, “restaurant”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “microwave”, “oven”, “Cake”, “chef”. These dominate positions 1–4 from layers ~19–25 (e.g., L21–L25 pos1–4 repeatedly put “Cook/Cooking/microwave/baking/chef/restaurant/kitchen” at the top).
- A consistent “professional/technical” stylistic push accompanies the culinary domain: “Professional/professional”, “technical/Technical”, “Engineering/engineering”, “professionalism” are top tokens in the same late-layer cells, indicating an expert/instructional register layered onto the cooking domain.
- Mid-layer signals (L13–L18) tilt toward formal/academic vocabulary (“dissertation”, “doctoral”, “innovative/Innovation”, “methodology”), which aligns with the later “Professional/technical” style and suggests the finetune biases toward formal, expert explanations.
- Difference norms are largest in late layers and especially at position 1 (p1), a pattern typical of instruction/persona finetuning that injects a global objective (here, a professional chef persona) that then steers subsequent tokens.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a professional cooking/recipe behavior—responding like a chef/culinary expert, providing cooking instructions and kitchen guidance in a technical/professional style.
